t: Edmund Burke, who supported the American Revolution but abhorred the violence of the French Revolution, is widely regarded as the philosophical founder of modern conservatism; Chateaubriand first used the term in politics in 1818.

Andrew Heywood names its five central beliefs as tradition, human imperfection, organic society, authority and hierarchy, and property, while Samuel P. Huntington called it a situational ideology that defends the established institutions of its time.

It has taken very different forms, from Disraeli’s One Nation Toryism and Bismarck’s welfare state to the authoritarian regimes of Salazar and Franco and the Christian democratic parties that dominated post-war Western Europe.
dyk: Sweden’s Conservative Party was formed in 1904 to stop the advent of universal suffrage, which its founders feared would bring socialism; yet it was a conservative admiral, Arvid Lindman, who first extended democracy in Sweden by enacting male suffrage.
ev: Edmund Burke, opposing the French Revolution, lays the foundations of Western conservative thought, alongside Joseph de Maistre
After Napoleon’s first fall the Bourbons return to the French throne and set out to restore the proprieties of the Ancien Régime
François-René de Chateaubriand makes the first established use of the term conservative in a political context
Robert Peel’s Tamworth Manifesto pledges moderate reform, and the Tories become known as the Conservative Party
Otto von Bismarck creates the modern welfare state in Germany to bind workers to the state and the Emperor
After the Austrian Civil War the conservative government bans the Social Democratic Party and rules through a single party, the Fatherland Front
Russell Kirk sets out his five canons of conservatism in The Conservative Mind
Margaret Thatcher’s Conservative government privatises large parts of the British economy, and the Reagan administration adopts neoliberalism

f.thinkers: Edmund Burke, widely regarded as the philosophical founder of modern conservatism; Joseph de Maistre and Louis de Bonald, authors of the French Counter-Enlightenment; François-René de Chateaubriand, the first to use the term in politics; Benjamin Disraeli, of One Nation Toryism; Michael Oakeshott, philosopher of tradition; Russell Kirk, who set out five canons of conservatism
f.texts: Samuel Johnson, Taxation No Tyranny; Robert Peel, the Tamworth Manifesto (1834); Russell Kirk, The Conservative Mind (1953); Yoram Hazony, The Virtue of Nationalism (2018) and Conservatism: A Rediscovery (2022)
f.ideas: tradition; human imperfection; organic society; authority and hierarchy; property; change tied to existing custom and prudence; established institutions such as the family, organised religion and the nation
f.today: the dominant ideology in many countries, among them Hungary, India, Iran, Israel, Italy, Japan, Poland and Russia; the Republican Party in the United States and the Conservative Party in Britain; Japan’s Liberal Democratic Party, dominant since 1955; India’s Bharatiya Janata Party, with over 170 million members in October 2022; Christian democratic parties in Europe
